books.section: Topic 6.6 The Rise of Industrial Capitalism
Industrialization, Corporate Consolidation, and the Gospel of Wealth

options.text: The catalog brought the store to distant farm families

options.misconception: Farm families bought from catalogs, so they had money to spend; distance was the problem.
options.text: Farm families had no money to buy anything

options.misconception: Distance kept farm families from stores; they did not refuse to go.
options.text: Farm families refused to visit towns

options.misconception: Background: catalogs sold goods; they were not the only books in farm homes.
options.text: Catalogs were the only books farm families owned

rationales.A: Background from the books: being far from a city was no longer a barrier, because catalogs let farm families order goods and railroads delivered them.
rationales.B: Farm families ordered goods through the catalogs, which shows they had money to spend. Their problem was distance, not poverty alone.
rationales.C: The books say distance was the barrier, not refusal. Catalogs solved the distance.
rationales.D: Background: catalogs were sales books, not the only reading in farm homes. Their value was in ordering goods.
rationales.general:
Ask what problem the catalog solved.
1. Farm families lived far from cities and their stores.
2. Background from the books: a catalog let them choose goods without traveling to a store.
3. Railroads then carried the ordered goods to the farm.
4. Together the catalog and the railroad closed the distance.
Remember: a new way of selling matters most to the people the old way left out.

source: original; stimulus verified against its source (see source_note)
stem: Why did mail-order catalogs matter most to farm families?

stimulus.text: A stereoscopic view of the Montgomery Ward and Company establishment in Chicago, a huge multi-story building with a tall tower rising over the neighboring blocks. The caption calls it “one of the sights of the city,” and the building’s many windows show floor after floor of goods.
